# Data-quality notes (generated by scripts/01_eda.py)

* The .route file lists the arcs in driving order but does not say which GPS point belongs to which arc. Point labels are created with a monotone dynamic-programming alignment (src/pathsnap/labels.py). Overall 88.6% of GPS points get a reference segment within 30 m.
* 4 trip(s) where > 10 % of GPS points have no reference segment within 30 m: 00000002 (GPS track 55.9 km vs reference route 8.0 km); 00000033 (GPS track 47.8 km vs reference route 6.4 km); 00000043 (GPS track 63.7 km vs reference route 59.2 km); 00000054 (GPS track 169.3 km vs reference route 31.4 km). The reference route covers only part of the GPS track (e.g. repeated loops or driving that the route omits). Such points are excluded from training labels and metrics instead of being forced onto a wrong segment.
* 23 trip(s) contain time gaps > 60 s (max 153064 s): 00000002, 00000006, 00000011, 00000014, 00000021, 00000024, 00000028, 00000041, 00000042, 00000043, 00000044, 00000054, 00000055, 00000069, 00000070, 00000078, 00000081, 00000084, 00000085, 00000088, 00000089, 00000090, 00000065. The HMM starts a new segment across such gaps.
* 23 trip(s) have implied speeds > 200 km/h between consecutive points (GPS jumps): 00000001, 00000005, 00000008, 00000013, 00000024, 00000028, 00000031, 00000032, 00000033, 00000042, 00000043, 00000053, 00000055, 00000057, 00000079, 00000085, 00000092, 00000093, 00000096, 00000098, 00000000, 00000040, 00000056.
* 14 trip(s) with < 90 % of steps at exactly 1 s: 00000004, 00000014, 00000018, 00000022, 00000025, 00000026, 00000039, 00000046, 00000071, 00000078, 00000081, 00000090, 00000098, 00000076.
* Non-finite GPS rows across all trips: 0; non-increasing timestamps: 0.
* Road networks contain isolated nodes in 0 trips; median number of weakly connected components = 19.
* Reference routes are continuous (arc[i].to == arc[i+1].from) for 99.94% of consecutive pairs on average; min trip continuity = 98.13%.
* Trips are spread across many countries, each with its own local road network, so all distances are computed in a per-trip local metric projection.
